the development of new test methods for the characterization of the TLU susceptibility of CMOS devices.
the development of new methods for the detection and characterization of latch-up in CMOS devices, which can also be applied at wafer-level.
the development and application of a test method to study the latch-up phenomenon triggered by transient signals of short duration.

we have demonstrated the possibility to trigger and detect TLU in CMOS devices at wafer level and package level using a TLU-module with a short pulse generator as a stress source.
the presented TLU-method is a powerful tool to identify latch-up susceptible ICs and ICs that are immune to transient latch-up.
the TLU-method is a valuable tool to identify latch-up sensitive CMOS devices, to study their latch-up characteristics and to optimize the design of the devices and the layout.

the TLU test setup can be used to study TLU susceptibility at wafer and package level, and that it allows to study the latch-up behavior of devices with very high speed.
